subject: Apex Integrations — SDK v1 deprecation / compatibility shim coordination
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@apexintegrations.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Upcoming Apex SDK v1 removal — call for coordination

Hi Vanessa,

Heads up — our engineering team is planning to remove the legacy SDK v1 bindings on 2027-03-01. We discovered a few call surface changes in Redwood's hosted API between v1 and the newer model-serving endpoints that will break our automation.

Attached are: 1) apex_integration_notes.pdf (high-level list of breakages) and 2) a short compatibility matrix (compat_matrix.xlsx) we started.

Can we align on a short window for:
- a compatibility shim or interim adapter from Redwood's side, or
- clear deprecation date + migration guidance if a shim is not possible?

We'd like to avoid a hard cut that would impact our customers. Evan

--
Evan Brooks
Head of Integrations, Apex Integrations
https://www.apexintegrations.com
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@apexintegrations.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming Apex SDK v1 removal — call for coordination

Hi Evan — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We opened this with our runtime team and put together an initial plan.

Quick proposal:
- Redwood provides a lightweight compatibility shim for the most common v1 call patterns for 90 days after your removal date (2027-03-01 -> 2027-05-01).
- During that 90-day window, Apex runs migration tests against a canary endpoint we will expose; Redwood will commit to one patch release per week for shim fixes.
- After 90 days the shim will be deprecated; we will provide a migration guide and an automated lint tool to surface changes.

Can you confirm the list of endpoints and the priority usage patterns (batch vs streaming vs embeddings)? Also please confirm you can allocate a small test team for the canary.

I'll book a 30-minute sync for Wed to triage.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | partner@redwood.ai
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@apexintegrations.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming Apex SDK v1 removal — call for coordination

Hey team — technical note from runtime side.

Summary of feasibility: we can implement a compatibility shim that maps the v1 client calls to the new runtime routes with a small adapter layer. Limitations to call out:
- Streaming sessions: the shim can support server-sent chunking but we may need Apex to relax strict framing expectations during the canary.
- Tokenization edge cases: some early models used a legacy tokenizer flow; the shim will emulate the tokens for the top-10 most common model configs only.

Proposed timeline (engineering):
- Week 1 (by 2027-02-24): prototype shim + internal smoke tests.
- Week 2 (by 2027-03-03): canary endpoint + basic docs, shared with Apex test team.
- Weeks 3-6: iterative fixes based on test failures; weekly patch cadence.

Risks & mitigations:
- If Apex has proprietary call patterns not in the top-10, those will need small client-side changes. We'll document exact API differences in apex_sdk_diff.md.
- If performance regressions appear, we'll support a dedicated routing policy for Apex traffic for short-term capacity isolation.

I'll attach apex_sdk_diff.md once prototype tests run. Sergio

--
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@apexintegrations.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming Apex SDK v1 removal — call for coordination

Thanks — that timeline is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Priority endpoints: batch inference (heavy), real-time streaming (medium), and embeddings (low).
- We can relax framing on streaming during the canary, but need a clear rollback plan in case data mismatch occurs.
- We ran a quick scan; two of our internal wrappers depend on the legacy tokenization behavior — I'll enumerate those in the compat matrix by EOD.

Can we get access to the canary endpoint the week of 2027-03-01? Our devs will run smoke tests and report back in a shared spreadsheet.

Attaching the initial compat matrix export. Evan

Attachment: compat_matrix.xlsx (stub)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@apexintegrations.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2027 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upcoming Apex SDK v1 removal — call for coordination

Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for adding priority info. Finalizing next steps here so everyone has a single source of truth:

Action items:
- Redwood (Sergio): deliver prototype shim and apex_sdk_diff.md by 2027-02-24.
- Apex (Evan): complete compat_matrix.xlsx with the two legacy wrapper calls called out by 2027-02-22 EOD.
- Redwood (Marissa): provision canary endpoint and invite Apex to test week of 2027-03-01; will provide access instructions.
- Vanessa: run a 30-minute sync on 2027-02-23 10:00 PT to triage any outstanding flags (calendar invite sent).

Docs & links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/apex-sdk-transition-plan (contains migration guide draft, apex_sdk_diff.md when available, and test checklist).

Sign-off needed by both parties to proceed with the 90-day compatibility shim approach. If Apex prefers not to use a shim, please indicate by the 2027-02-23 sync so we can switch to a coordinated lift-and-migrate schedule.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
